title: capsule-registry (Home-2) Registry Entry
description: Machine-checkable shape for one Home-2 semantics filing. Fill in registry/entries/TEMPLATE.yaml, save it as registry/entries/<name>.yaml, add its record schema under registry/schemas/<name>.schema.json and its example records under registry/entries/examples/<name>/{positive,boundary,must-fail}.json, then open a PR. .github/validate_registry_entries.py validates this file against this schema, validates each declared example's extracted record against the entry's own record schema, runs each example's full capsule through agent-action-capsule verify, and rejects the entry if any of those checks doesn't match the example's declared `expected` block. This is the machine-checkable half of REGISTRATION-POLICY.md; that document remains the normative prose description of the lifecycle. Ported from scitt-payload-binding's CPB registry filing tooling (PR #77, branch head e136bf8, itself HELD pending Steven+Anton ratification as of the port) -- see PROVENANCE.md for the exact source commit and what changed for Home-2's own ruling.

name.description: The controlled identifier this entry registers. Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Matches the entry file's own name (registry/entries/<name>.yaml) and its examples directory (registry/entries/examples/<name>/).

kind.description: Which REGISTRY.md reserved section (or, for record-schema, which future section) this entry targets. record-schema is for a capsule subject-block shape with its own closed vocabulary (e.g. a mesh card) that doesn't reduce to a single slot-profile/action-type/outcome/purpose-label/pack value.

status.description: REGISTRATION-POLICY.md's two-state lifecycle. There is no Designated Expert ladder in Home-2 (unlike CPB's Home-1) -- promotion is Steven's (or the spec-tier gate's, once delegated) per-entry ruling, never a batch operation and never inferred from a sibling entry's promotion.

owner.description: Who is asserting this convention -- the repo/team whose code or spec text this entry is filing from.

reference.description: Where this convention actually lives: a repository reference MUST carry a commit hash (a branch or tag alone is not a pin) plus a path, e.g. 'action-state-group/capsule-emit-mesh @ <full-commit-hash> -- join_card.py'.

home1_reference.description: The CPB (Home-1) Artifact Type / Algorithm entry, or its provisional-registry entry, that carries this name's Digest Context table -- cited BY NAME, never duplicated (REGISTRY.md's within-entry rule). null when this entry has no mechanical counterpart registered or provisional in CPB yet -- that is an honest 'nothing to cite' per REGISTRY.md, not an error, but should be named in open_questions if one is expected to appear later.

path.description: Path, relative to the repository root, to this entry's declared JSON Schema. Validates the SEMANTIC content only -- vocabulary, closed enums, producer invariants -- never a Digest Context table (that is Home-1's job, cited via home1_reference).

record_path.description: The key path, inside an example's full capsule (`record` in the example file), locating the semantic subject block the schema above validates. An empty array means the whole `record` value IS the subject (no capsule envelope to unwrap).

closed_enums.description: Every closed enum this entry registers, with its values' meanings spelled out (REGISTRATION-POLICY.md requires an entry name its semantic content, not just point at code). Optional only for a kind that genuinely has no enum (e.g. a pack namespace claim).

verifier_expectations.description: What grade/state a conforming example yields when run through `agent-action-capsule verify` (Steven's 2026-09-05 ruling: examples are validating records run through the reference verifier, not CPB-style digest fixtures). State the expected `ok` value and any expected finding codes/severities in prose -- .github/validate_registry_entries.py checks the machine-readable `expected` block inside each example file, not this prose, but a human reviewer needs the prose to judge whether the machine-readable expectation is the RIGHT one.

examples_dir.description: Path, relative to the repository root, to this entry's examples. Must contain positive.json, boundary.json, and must-fail.json (Registration Rule: two-sided coverage, mirroring CPB's positive/negative discipline, plus a boundary case). Each file is {kind, expected: {record_schema_valid, verify_ok, notes}, record: <the example capsule or bare record>}.

open_questions.description: Every unresolved question this entry still carries. Required key (may be an empty array) so a reviewer never has to infer whether something was simply forgotten versus deliberately left open. Never filled in by a CPB/AAC editor on the filer's behalf.

promoted_by.description: Required when status=promoted: 'Steven / spec-tier ruling, <date>'. Omit entirely for a provisional entry.
